chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) issued a ruling in the flood of Wadi Mahzur that the upper (water source) is held for the lower (fields) for palm trees up to two 'ikb (forearms), and for crops up to two 'sharak (ankles).

key_terms.الشِّرَاكَيْنِ: Two ankles (a unit of measurement for water depth)
key_terms.الْكَعْبَيْنِ: Two forearms (a unit of measurement for water depth)
key_terms.وَادِي مَهْزُور: Wadi Mahzur, a specific location mentioned in the narration
key_terms.يُحْبَس: To be held back or retained (for use)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on water distribution for agriculture during floods?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith details the Prophet’s judicial ruling in Wadi Mahzur, establishing a precedent for equitable water distribution in agricultural communities. It specifies that upper landowners must retain water up to a depth of two forearms for date palms and two ankles for crops, ensuring sufficient flow reaches lower fields. This ruling underscores the Shia legal principle of preventing harm (*darar*) and prioritizing communal welfare in resource management.
